messages:
sam: Hey all 44b day 1 question. I downloaded the kubeconfig and can `kubectl config get-contexts` fine, but when I try `kubectl get pods -n team-ml` I get 
``
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:default:default" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "team-ml"
``
It looks like I'm hitting the cluster as a serviceaccount? I set up Okta SSO earlier. Who should I ask to bind me to the right role?

infra-bot: Access request #AK-16021 created for user sam. Approver: @raj. Status: pending. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-16021

lucy: welcome @sam! That error means your kubeconfig is using a serviceaccount token (common if you downloaded a pod-mounted token or used `kubectl --token` by accident). First run `kubectl config view --raw` and look at the user entry for your current context to confirm. If it shows `token:` with a short base64 string, that's the issue. Should show an `exec` block for OIDC.

sam: `kubectl config view --raw` shows user `sam-local` with `token:` indeed. I must have grabbed the wrong file from home backups. Re-downloading OIDC kubeconfig now.

raj: quick note on RBAC: we avoid creating ClusterRoleBindings for user dev access. We create a Role in the namespace and bind it to an AD group (e.g., `team-ml-devs`). If your manager approves, we add you to that group and create a RoleBinding. I can approve the ticket but need manager confirmation for group membership. If manager is offline, we have an auto-approve policy for first-day sandbox access for 48h. @terra-bot can you check and apply?

terra-bot: Auto-approve check: user sam is new-hire within 7 days. Manager approval required? unknown. Applying temporary onboarding binding: created RoleBinding `onboard-sam-team-ml` binding AD group `onboard-temp` to Role `developer` in namespace `team-ml` for 48h. Ticket AK-16021 updated.

sam: after re-downloading OIDC kubeconfig, `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-ml` still returns `no`. The auto-bind is neat but curious why cluster still says no.

lucy: run `kubectl config current-context` and then `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="'"$(kubectl config current-context)"'" )].context.user}'` to get which user entry is used. Then `kubectl auth can-i --as system:serviceaccount:onboard-temp list pods -n team-ml` to check the temporary binding permissions. Also make sure your context user matches your OIDC user (github/AD mapping). Sometimes people keep an old `user` name referencing a token entry.

sam: current-context is `redwood-dev@redwood-cluster`. The user name is `sam-oidc`. `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-ml` -> `no`. `kubectl auth can-i --as system:serviceaccount:onboard-temp list pods -n team-ml` -> `yes`.

raj: that tells us the RoleBinding is correct but your OIDC identity isn't mapped to the `onboard-temp` group. Lucy, can you check AD group mapping for sam?

lucy: checking... AD mapping shows `onboard-temp` contains `onboard:sam-temp` serviceaccount and no OIDC user. I think terra created a serviceaccount-based temporary binding (my mistake). I'll update the ticket to create a RoleBinding to the AD group `onboard-temp-users` and add your GitHub handle to that group. @sam DM your GitHub handle?

sam: dm'd: samcodes

lucy: done. I updated the RoleBinding to reference the AD group `onboard-temp-users` rather than the serviceaccount. Please wait a minute for group sync. Meanwhile to avoid repetitive `-n` use this: `kubectl config set-context sam-team-ml --namespace=team-ml --cluster=redwood-dev@redwood-cluster --user=sam-oidc && kubectl config use-context sam-team-ml`.

sam: group sync propagated. `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-ml` -> `yes` now. I can `kubectl get pods` and port-forward a svc. Thanks! Quick extra Q: who do we ping if the onboarding RoleBindings should become permanent?

raj: ping me and file a ticket in https://redwood.internal/infra-requests with the justification (team membership + recurring access). We try to move people from `onboard-temp` to team groups after 2-4 weeks. Also avoid using serviceaccount tokens locally; always use OIDC. Welcome to the team, @sam :tada:

sam: thanks everyone! super smooth onboarding. One last note: lucy, the terraform RBAC module name would be handy in the ticket so I can reference it for perms.
